summary:
Space Heritage Explorer is an interactive 3D planetary heritage museum that brings humanity's historic space exploration missions to life. The platform allows users to explore the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space through immersive 3D environments, discover documented spacecraft and exploration equipment, and understand the stories behind humanity's journey beyond Earth.

Users can interact with planetary surfaces, explore historical mission locations, inspect spacecraft models, and access detailed mission records, including launch and landing dates, landing coordinates, mission objectives, equipment status, and scientific contributions.

By combining 3D visualization, historical mission data, scientific resources, and interactive storytelling, Space Heritage Explorer transforms scattered space exploration records into an engaging educational experience. It highlights the legacy of spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments, including equipment that remains on other worlds long after their missions have ended.

Our goal is to preserve humanity's space exploration heritage and make the history, achievements, and lasting impact of planetary exploration accessible to everyone.
details:
SPACE HERITAGE EXPLORER

An Interactive 3D Museum of Humanity's Space Exploration Legacy

1. Project Overview

Space Heritage Explorer is an interactive, web-based 3D planetary heritage platform designed to document, visualize and communicate humanity's exploration beyond Earth. It brings together three major exploration environments — the Moon, Mars and Deep Space — allowing users to discover historical space missions, spacecraft, planetary landing locations and exploration equipment through an immersive digital experience.

The primary objective is to transform scattered space exploration information into an accessible and engaging educational platform where users can understand not only where humanity has explored, but also the missions, technologies and scientific achievements behind those explorations.

2. Our Proposed Solution

The platform is organized into three exploration modules:

A. Moon Explorer

Provides an interactive 3D lunar environment featuring historical lunar exploration missions, including Apollo missions and Surveyor spacecraft. Users can explore documented mission locations, select individual missions and examine available spacecraft information, mission details and associated equipment.

B. Mars Explorer

Provides a 3D representation of Mars featuring robotic exploration missions, including Viking, Mars Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight and Ingenuity. The module presents mission histories, exploration locations and the achievements of robotic systems that helped expand our understanding of Mars.

C. Deep Space Explorer

Provides a solar-system exploration interface featuring spacecraft and missions that have travelled beyond planetary surfaces. Examples include Pioneer 10, Dawn and NEAR Shoemaker. Users can explore mission information and understand the significance of humanity's robotic exploration of distant celestial environments.

3. How the Platform Works

The user enters through the Earth Hub and selects one of the three exploration destinations. The platform loads the corresponding interactive 3D environment. Users can rotate and zoom the planetary visualization, explore mission markers, select spacecraft or mission records and access detailed information.

The exploration process follows:

Destination Selection → 3D Exploration → Mission Selection → Spacecraft and Equipment Information → Historical Storytelling → Scientific Legacy.

The platform does not require user authentication, allowing visitors to access the experience directly.

4. Technology Stack

The project uses a modern web development architecture:

  • Frontend: React 18, TypeScript and Vite.
  • Navigation: React Router 6.
  • 3D Rendering: Three.js and React Three Fiber.
  • 3D Utilities: Drei.
  • Model Optimization: Draco WASM compression.
  • Database: Supabase PostgreSQL with JSONB mission records.
  • Data Processing: Python 3 ETL workflows.
  • UI Development: Tailwind CSS and Lucide Icons.
  • Asset Delivery: Cloud Storage and CDN.

The architecture is designed to support interactive 3D environments, structured mission information and optimized delivery of planetary textures and 3D assets.

5. NASA Data and Research Resources

Our research and resource collection includes official NASA and planetary science resources:

  • NASA National Space Science Data Center (NSSDC).
  • NASA Science Mission Archives.
  • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS).
  • NASA 3D Resources.
  • NASA Images.
  • Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) archives.
  • Mars Raw Images Repository.
  • NASA's catalogue of human-made material on the Moon.
  • NASA/JPL Photojournal.

Additional planetary resources include USGS Astrogeology, USGS planetary datasets and the HiRISE Planetary Data System.

These resources provide mission references, planetary imagery, historical records, scientific information and potential 3D assets for the platform. Individual resources are being organized for accurate attribution and future integration.

6. Innovation and Impact

The main innovation of Space Heritage Explorer is its combination of interactive planetary visualization and mission-based storytelling.

Instead of presenting space exploration as a conventional collection of text and photographs, the platform creates a navigable digital museum connecting planetary environments with historical missions and their equipment.

It aims to:

  • Preserve and communicate humanity's planetary exploration heritage.
  • Improve public understanding of historical space missions.
  • Make planetary science more accessible to students and educators.
  • Encourage interest in astronomy, aerospace engineering and scientific research.
  • Highlight the scientific and historical importance of exploration equipment.

7. Future Development

Our next development phase will focus on expanding the platform with:

  • Detailed 3D models of individual abandoned spacecraft and scientific instruments.
  • Artifact-level historical records and documented equipment conditions.
  • Original NASA photographs and evidence-linked mission stories.
  • Interactive historical timelines and mission event sequences.
  • Improved guided museum and educational storytelling modes.
  • More detailed lunar and Martian surface visualizations.
  • Additional verified mission records and planetary datasets.
  • Improved accessibility, mobile optimization and performance.

8. Our Vision

Space Heritage Explorer aims to become an interactive digital archive of humanity's journey beyond Earth.

Every spacecraft represents an achievement, every landing site represents a milestone, and every piece of equipment tells a story of exploration.

Our vision is to ensure that these achievements remain discoverable, understandable and inspiring for future generations.

Their missions may have ended, but their discoveries live on.
